steps.note: Add the foreign key as NOT VALID: from now on every inserted/updated order must reference an existing customer, without scanning the 10M existing rows. This needs a brief SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE lock on orders and customers, so take it with a short lock_timeout (app queries have a 2 s statement timeout) and retry instead of queueing behind a long transaction. Skipped if the constraint already exists.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'orders_customer_id_fkey' AND conrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass) THEN RETURN; END IF; FOR i IN 1..30 LOOP BEGIN PERFORM set_config('lock_timeout', '300ms', true); ALTER TABLE public.orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES public.customers (id) NOT VALID; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(1); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders/customers to add orders_customer_id_fkey after 30 tries'; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the existing rows. VALIDATE CONSTRAINT only takes SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on orders (ROW SHARE on customers), so the app keeps reading and inserting during the 10M-row scan. No statement timeout for this long scan. If any pre-existing order points at a missing customer, this fails and the plan stops with the constraint still enforced for new rows (live check before planning found 0 orphans).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; SET lock_timeout = '10s'; ALTER TABLE public.orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey;

steps.note: Verify the foreign key exists and is validated.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'orders_customer_id_fkey' AND conrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND contype = 'f' AND convalidated) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders_customer_id_fkey missing or not validated'; END IF; END $$;
